title: Why Is Pinterest (PINS) Down 9.2% Since Last Earnings Report?
author: Na
description: Pinterest reported Q2 2026 earnings of 43 cents per share, beating estimates by 19.44%, with revenues up 18% year-over-year to $1.18 billion. The company achieved record user growth of 640 million monthly active users and expanded AI-powered advertising capabilities. Despite a 9.2% share decline over the past month, Pinterest raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to 30% and generated strong free cash flow of $270 million.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Pinterest exceeded earnings expectations by 19.44%, achieved record user growth for the 12th consecutive quarter (640M MAUs, +11% YoY), expanded EBITDA margins to 26%, and raised full-year guidance. Strong AI-driven advertising momentum and improved monetization across geographies support positive outlook, though recent stock performance has lagged the S&P 500.

Meta reported strong revenue growth of 28% YoY to $60.8 billion, but EPS declined from $7.14 to $6.18. Current quarter earnings expected to decline 12.7% YoY. Stock gained only 0.7% over the past month and holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a C VGM Score, indicating in-line performance expectations.

title: Opinion: Google's Latest Antitrust Ruling Is a Big Win for Alphabet Investors
author: Patrick Sanders
description: A federal judge rejected the DOJ's request to force Google to sell parts of its ad-tech business, allowing Alphabet to keep its powerful advertising engine intact. This decision mirrors a similar ruling one year ago that preceded a 16% stock jump. The ruling is significant as Alphabet's $81.63 billion advertising revenue is critical for funding its massive AI infrastructure investments.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Judge rejected DOJ's forced divestiture request, preserving Alphabet's lucrative $81.63B advertising business which funds critical AI capex spending. Historical precedent shows similar ruling led to 16% stock jump, suggesting positive investor sentiment and removal of significant business risk.

title: Hims & Hers Health (NYSE: HIMS) Faces Securities Class Action After FTC Lawsuit Reveal Drives Stock Sharply Lower -- HBSS
author: Hagens Berman
description: Hims & Hers Health (NYSE: HIMS) faces a securities class action lawsuit following an FTC complaint alleging the company engaged in deceptive health data sharing with advertising platforms like Meta and Snap, and violated billing regulations by charging consumers for prescriptions before medical consultations. The lawsuit, filed by the FTC alongside Utah and Los Angeles County, also accuses Hims of using dark patterns to prevent subscription cancellations. The stock dropped 14.7% ($4.32) on July 29, 2026, erasing over $970 million in market value.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company faces serious regulatory allegations including deceptive data sharing with third-party advertisers, unauthorized subscription billing, and dark pattern cancellation practices. Stock declined 14.7% on lawsuit announcement, and company faces potential significant financial penalties and reputational damage.
Meta is mentioned as a recipient of shared health data through tracking pixels but is not the subject of the lawsuit. No direct allegations or impact on Meta's operations are stated.

title: Nvidia Did the Heavy Lifting for the Major Market Indexes Today
author: Anders Bylund
description: Major market indexes rose modestly by 0.4% on Wednesday, with Nvidia and Meta Platforms driving nearly all gains. Nvidia jumped 3.8% to $225.67, single-handedly contributing 0.38% to the Nasdaq Composite's gain. Without these two stocks, the Nasdaq would be down and the S&P 500 would be nearly flat. Market moves were driven by macroeconomic factors, including New York Fed President John Williams' comments on Treasury yields reflecting a strong economy driven by AI and data center investment.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock surged 3.8% to $225.67, creating $206 billion in market value and single-handedly driving 0.38% of the Nasdaq Composite's gains. Strong performance reflects investor confidence in AI and data center investments.
Stock jumped 2.9%, contributing significantly to index gains alongside Nvidia. Positive price movement indicates investor confidence, though no specific company news drove the gain.

title: Why The Trade Desk Stock Rallied Today
author: Danny Vena, Cpa
description: The Trade Desk stock surged 4.9% after the FTC and 22 states filed suit against Amazon for allegedly using deceptive ad pricing practices, including undisclosed surcharges. This legal action highlights The Trade Desk's competitive advantage through transparent pricing and could help the company recapture market share from competitors with closed ecosystems.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock rallied 4.9% on news of competitor's legal troubles. The lawsuit against Amazon highlights The Trade Desk's transparent pricing advantage and could help it recapture advertising dollars from closed ecosystems, though the company still faces structural headwinds from six consecutive quarters of decelerating growth.

Facing FTC lawsuit from 22 states alleging deceptive ad practices including undisclosed surcharges and concealed auction costs. Amazon denies the charges but the legal action creates reputational risk and potential regulatory consequences.
